key_insight: Hyperspectral imaging can non-destructively separate donor and acceptor signals in roll-to-roll slot-die coated organic photovoltaic active layers, enabling real-time inline quality monitoring.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable metrology approach for process control in high-throughput organic solar cell manufacturing, supporting consistent coating quality during roll-to-roll production.
method: Inline hyperspectral camera captures spatially resolved absorbance during coating.
Multivariate curve resolution separates P3HT donor and OIDTBR acceptor contributions.
Spectral fitting of P3HT absorbance maps exciton bandwidth to probe aggregation and chain interactions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful spatial resolution of donor and acceptor distributions and extraction of exciton bandwidth from P3HT spectra in a roll-to-roll setup.
watch_item: Inline hyperspectral monitoring may require robust calibration and spectral deconvolution to remain reliable under changing coating conditions and production noise.
paper_title: Hyperspectral imaging for inline quality monitoring of roll-to-roll slot-die coated organic photovoltaic active layers
